newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU worried about Japan trade surplus - Brittan.
newsitem.headline: EU worried about Japan trade surplus - Brittan.

text.p: The European Union is worried about Japan's expanding trade surplus, European Commissioner Leon Brittan said on Wednesday.
A Japanese government spokesman said Brittan had expressed his concern at the annual EU-Japan summit here.
"Brittan told Hashimoto that Europe is worried about the recent expansion of Japan's trade surplus as there were very troublesome surplus problems in the past," he said.

The spokesman said Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto had told Brittan and other European officials that Japan's trade surplus was on a firm declining trend despite temporary increases in recent months.
Hashimoto had also said in the summit meeting that he hoped the euro would start as a firm currency, the spokesman said.
EU worried about Japan trade surplus - Brittan =3
The spokesman quoted Brittan, the EU Trade Commissioner, as saying that Japan and the European Union had cooperated in various economic areas and had achieved progress.
He said Brittan had called on Japan to expand the scope of its deregulation efforts and that in reply Hashimoto had urged the EU to carry out deregulation too.

The Japanese spokesman also quoted European Commission President Jacques Santer as saying there should be no delay in the introduction of the EU's single currency, the euro, which is sheduled to be launched in January 1999.
